takeaways.label: ARR-heavy profit engine delivers 29% PAT growth
takeaways.text: Group after-tax profit hit ₹718 crores, driven by Asset and Private Wealth businesses which grew 43% YoY and now contribute 58% of operating profit, up from 49% last year.

takeaways.label: AMC hits critical mass with flows and performance
takeaways.text: AUM crossed ₹2.23 lakh crores, net flow market share at 6% is more than double the AUM share of 2.7%, and 99% of AUM outperforms the benchmark over three years, setting up a powerful flywheel as more funds cross the three-year vintage mark.

takeaways.label: Private wealth AUM surged 58% YoY but profit growth paused
takeaways.text: AUM reached ₹2.96 lakh crores with net flows up 65% QoQ, yet Q2 PAT rose only 2% YoY on a high base; management expects H2 growth to be much higher as RM productivity from recent hires kicks in.

takeaways.label: Carry income becomes a recurring, predictable stream
takeaways.text: Carry income jumped from ~₹65 cr to ~₹108 cr this quarter as select funds hit recognition thresholds, and management now calls it more predictable than ARR income given the long duration of funds and the nature of booking.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether AMC net flow momentum holds above ₹2,000 cr per month, the pace of private wealth PAT re-acceleration in H2, and any initial signals on the custodian business product strategy ahead of its Q4 launch.

sections.title: The ARR Transformation: Twin-Engine Model Delivers

points.label: ARR revenue share jumped to 66%
points.text: of group revenues, up from 55% in FY24, as Asset and Private Wealth profit after tax grew 44% YoY, structurally reducing the group's dependence on cyclical transaction businesses.

points.label: Asset and Private Wealth now drive 58% of operating profit
points.text: , up from 49% in FY26 and 42% in FY25, because these businesses carry strong structural tailwinds and have consistently outgrown the rest of the group.

points.label: Non-broking revenue in wealth management hit 65%
points.text: in H1 FY27 versus 53% in FY24, led by comprehensive asset management offerings and strong performance across all businesses, shifting the franchise away from pure brokerage dependence.

points.label: The large investment book acts as a backbone
points.text: to all operating businesses, absorbing regulatory changes, funding rising business needs, and supporting market share gains across the group.

quotes.text: Navin Agarwal: "This has only been possible due to our unique twin-engine business model wherein our large investment book serves as a Strong backbone to all the operating businesses which have seen regulatory changes, rising funding needs, strong underlying business growth, and a market share gain."

sections.title: AMC: The Flow Flywheel Is Spinning

points.label: AUM reached a milestone ₹2.23 lakh crores
points.text: including MO Alternates, compounding at 32% over five years, with strong market share gains driven by fund performance rather than just product launches.

points.label: Net flow market share at 6% is more than double the AUM market share of 2.7%
points.text: , a gap management expects to persist because 99% of AUM outperforms the benchmark on a three-year basis, and six funds now have over three-year vintage with eight more crossing that threshold by March '28.

points.label: SIP flows hit ₹4,170 crores
points.text: with 4.4% market share, and SIP AUM stands at ₹42,000 crores, providing a stable base that compounds even when net active flows moderate temporarily.

points.label: Unique PANs crossed 1 crore
points.text: , meaning one in six mutual fund investors in India is now with Motilal Oswal AMC, a retail confidence signal that also widens the cross-sell funnel for the broader wealth franchise.

points.label: Net flows recovered sharply after a 2–3 month lean period
points.text: : September saw ₹2,400 cr net active inflows and October is expected over ₹2,000 cr, driven by 6% alpha generated last quarter, and management says the trend has definitely returned to earlier levels.

points.label: Several large funds cross the critical three-year vintage
points.text: over the next 6–7 months: small cap in December, large cap and multi-cap over the next three months, which matters because many distributors require a minimum three-year track record before allocating client money.

quotes.text: Prateek Agrawal: "Performance is a large part of what drives inflows, and with a very strong performance, you know, our funds did 6% kind of alpha last quarter, we believe traction in flows should continue."

sections.title: Private Wealth: AUM Surges, Profit Waits on RM Maturity

points.label: Private wealth AUM grew 58% YoY to ₹2.96 lakh crores
points.text: , with net flows up 65% QoQ to ₹6,357 crores and Q2 ARR revenue strong at ₹180 crores, yet Q2 PAT rose only 2% YoY because the base quarter last year was unusually high.

points.label: Only 33% of RMs have over three years of vintage
points.text: , while about 15% are under one year and not yet broken even; the rest have broken even, and management expects H2 PAT growth to be much higher than H1 as newer RMs mature and productivity rises.

points.label: ARR revenue in wealth management grew 10% YoY to ₹328 crores
points.text: , and the ARR share within the wealth franchise has nearly doubled from 33% in FY21 to 58% in Q2 FY27, mirroring the group-level shift toward recurring revenue.

points.label: Distribution book grew 26% YoY to ₹48,000 crores
points.text: and the loan book rose 42% YoY to ₹10,200 crores, with MTF market share close to 7% and expected to improve, while cross-sell penetration at 18% leaves significant headroom.

points.label: Transaction AUM saw a meaningful QoQ increase
points.text: driven by growth in custody assets as large promoter accounts transferred shareholdings into demat, plus MTF-driven broking assets, adding fee pools beyond pure advisory AUM.

sections.title: Alternates & Carry Income: The Next Decade's AMC

points.label: MO Alternates is positioned as the next structural growth driver
points.text: , with management comparing its current stage to where the mutual fund business was 10–15 years back, citing increasing fund sizes in every subsequent series and entry into newer categories like private credit and commercial offices.

points.label: Carry income jumped from ~₹65 cr to ~₹108 cr
points.text: this quarter because select mature funds progressed to a stage where recognition criteria are met and systematic approvals commenced, with accruals currently coming from largely two mature schemes.

points.label: Carry income is now described as more predictable than ARR income
points.text: , because the long duration of funds and the nature of booking create many quarters of visibility, and the variable annual return pool will keep rising with every quarter and year as IRR accruals get added and funds come closer to exit.

points.label: The maiden private credit fund of ₹3,000 crores
points.text: has crossed the 90% threshold with a pipeline exceeding the remaining 10%, and closure is being held back only to accommodate domestic institutional flows.

points.label: A maiden commercial offices real estate fund has been launched
points.text: , the fourth offering from the Alternates business, with closure expected over the next six months, and the number of product offerings will continue to rise every year across many white spaces.

quotes.text: Navin Agarwal: "This business is probably at the same stage of evolution as the mutual fund business was 10-15 years back."

sections.title: Broking & Institutional: Market Share Gains Despite Headwinds

points.label: Overall retail broking market share reached 7.9%
points.text: , with F&O premium share improving from 7.6% to 8.8% QoQ and cash market share improving from 6.8% to 8% QoQ, driven mainly by MTF book growth corresponding to market growth.

points.label: F&O share improved because the firm advises customers to play options safely
points.text: and tends to do better when market volumes are lower, a positioning that benefits from the current regulatory and market environment.

points.label: Regulatory changes and flat markets are now in the base
points.text: , and management expects broking revenue growth to improve going forward, though commodity brokerage yields fell sharply in the last two quarters as discount brokers entered commodities in a big way, causing a slight market-share impact that is expected to recover fast.

points.label: Investment banking closed 41 deals in H1
points.text: with ₹99,000 crores cumulative raise, fee income grew 39% QoQ to ₹94 crores, and the firm ranked #1 in QIPs and #3 in IPOs, with a strong pipeline and deal sizes larger than in the past.

points.label: Institutional Equirus crossed 400 companies under coverage
points.text: , on track for 500, which increases research depth and corporate engagement opportunities that feed the broader institutional franchise.

sections.title: Housing & Lending: Steady Growth, Improving Asset Quality

points.label: Housing finance disbursements grew 29% YoY to ₹701 crores
points.text: and AUM grew 24% YoY to ₹6,476 crores, with management expecting similar growth over the coming three years, supported by high capital adequacy and low leverage that remove the need for external equity.

points.label: All delinquency buckets are lower YoY
points.text: , though H1 is seasonally weaker with some increase; H2 is expected to see the bulk of recoveries and normalize GNPA to 1.1–1.2%, with further improvement from there.

points.label: The lending book's bulk growth came from the MTF book
points.text: for HNI and UHNI segments, largely in line with cash volume growth in the market, while the loan-against-shares portion is growing at roughly 20–25% a year.

points.label: Treasury investment book grew 27% YoY to ₹11,346 crores
points.text: , compounding at 41% since March 2014, driven by strong IRRs and reinvestment of operating profit, reinforcing the twin-engine model's backbone function.

items.title: AMC mutual fund franchise
items.text: AMC AUM crossed ₹2 lakh crores in August 2026 (₹2,22,812 cr at Sep'26, +26% YoY), with Q2FY27 SIP flows of ₹4,170 crores and net flow market share of 6% in September, roughly twice its 2.7% AUM share. Only six funds have 3+ year vintage today, rising to 16 by March '28 - mostly category-leading - which management expects to drive flows and diversify AUM; Asset Management already contributes 43% of group operating PAT, up from 31% a year earlier.

items.title: MO Alternates private credit and carry
items.text: The maiden ₹3,000 crore private credit fund has crossed the 90% threshold for final close, and a commercial offices real estate fund just launched with closure expected within six months; Alternates AUM is ₹23,091 cr at Sep'26, +36% YoY, with revenue up 92%. Carry income of ₹108 crores booked in Q2FY27 should multiply as more fund vintages mature through FY28-FY29, with only ~70% of fair value recognized so far.

items.title: Private Wealth Management scaling
items.text: PWM AUM rose 58% YoY to ₹2.96 lakh crores at Sep'26, with net flows up 65% QoQ and ARR revenue of ₹180 crores in Q2FY27; the RM base of 443 is only 33% three-year vintage, so productivity should improve as bankers season. The ₹7,333 crore UHNI lending book, up 90% YoY, is mostly LAS and MTF and still tiny relative to the client base, giving NII headroom over the next 2-3 years.

items.title: Wealth lending and MTF book
items.text: The group loan book rose 42% YoY to ₹10,197 crores at Sep'26, with the MTF book up 56% to ₹9,600+ crores and market share near 7% and expected to improve. MTF adoption among existing cash customers is only ~15%, and management expects NII to be a very important growth driver in FY27 given the AA+ rating and controlled gearing.

items.title: Investment banking deal pipeline
items.text: Investment banking closed 41 deals raising ₹99,000 crores in H1FY27 - including the LIC OFS and NSE IPO - with fee income up 39% QoQ to ₹94 crores and the #1 rank in QIPs. Management says signed mandates are substantial and deal sizes are getting bigger, positioning the business for strong YoY growth in FY27.

items.title: Custodian of securities licence
items.text: SEBI approved Motilal Oswal Custodial Services as Custodian of Securities on 23 Sep 2026 - the first such licence to a non-bank in over a decade - with operations starting in the last quarter of 2026 under a CEO hired from Deutsche Bank. The licence lets institutional clients - AIFs, PMS, mutual funds, insurers - get execution, custody and post-trade servicing in one relationship, adding a new Capital Markets lever from FY28 onward.

items.title: Pension fund (NPS) entry
items.text: PFRDA issued a Letter of Appointment dated 5 May 2026 naming MOAMC as Sponsor of a Pension Fund, and the wholly-owned entity Motilal Oswal Pension Fund Management was incorporated on 4 June 2026. The Certificate of Registration and Investment Management Agreement with NPS Trust are the remaining steps before full-scale operations, opening a long-duration AUM pool alongside the mutual fund business.

items.title: Housing finance Tier II/III expansion
items.text: MOHFL disbursements grew 29% YoY to ₹701 crores in Q2FY27 and AUM 24% to ₹6,476 crores, with management expecting similar growth over the coming three years and AUM doubling in 2-3 years on ~37.8% capital adequacy without external equity. The 126-branch network is expanding in Tier II/III first-time-buyer markets, and the AA+ upgrade should cut borrowing costs a further 15-20 bps over the next 12-18 months.
